calls.notes: Strong listening call with an experienced GC (mikvah building slab, two plunge pools, keyed stairs). Asked for plans, permit status, timeline and budget, matched his technical language, and got the plans moving to TC@ right away. Missed: no dated next step (when we send a range or meet on site), didn't ask bid due date or how many subs are bidding, and the name mix up (both Tim) cost a minute. Next time: close with a specific day for the range and a site meet.

Patient discovery on a scope that changed (variance fails, now ~2,000 SF garage addition or a metal building on a yard). Good positioning: KB-1 license, contractor-only engineer at about half the $12k he was quoted, and a realtor plus build package. Got size and his $150k to $200k expectation. Missed: Scott offered to pay for plans and a site walk, but no paid design agreement or date was set; the call wandered. Next time: lock a paid Phase 1 design step (like Crestview) and a dated site walk before hanging up.

Fast callback with a good credibility opener and solid scope (7x20 paver pad, HOA, ZIP fix) plus a clear pavers vs concrete explanation. Missed: gave $3,500 to $4,500 before asking budget, offered no lower option (smaller pad, simpler base, phasing) when he balked, then pointed him to a handyman and Home Depot and didn't book a visit; the follow-up text 'best price we can offer' closed the door. Next time: ask budget first, offer a good/better option, and book a quick visit to firm the price.

Quick, friendly Angi callback that booked the visit for Mon 5:30 PM around his two jobs, with a good credibility line (local Tucson family company, Angi top provider 10+ years) and an address check. Missed: no questions at all on driveway size, the asphalt tear-out, budget or timeline, and no ask for photos before a Tucson drive. Next time: two minutes of scope and budget questions and a photo request before booking.

Well structured: credibility opener, then access (single gate, wheelbarrow), spoils, gravel and permit questions, a clear spec (3,000 psi, rebar 36 in. OC) and a firm $3,200 price including a rush fee to beat his fence deadline. Missed: never asked budget before pricing, so the rush fee pushed it past what he expected and he pivoted to a wood deck; no value contrast beyond 'concrete lasts'. He passed by text an hour later. Next time: ask the budget first and offer a no-rush price next to the rush option.

Clear specs and two priced options on the call (8x12 about $3,000, 8x15 about $3,600), explained mix and rebar, promised a same-day proposal and Monday check-in, and followed through by text. Missed: long call with connection trouble, no budget or decision-timeline question, and no urgency or reason to choose us over the other bidder. She cancelled Wednesday's visit and hired someone else that afternoon.

Fast Angi callback with good golf rapport and a firm Monday 10 AM slot. Missed: zero qualification (paver vs. interlocking scope, size, budget, timing) before committing a Tucson trip, and no photo request. He cancelled Saturday ('going another direction'), and a reminder text still went out Sunday afterwards.

Patient discovery (sunken walkway squares from a water leak, new side walkway to the back patio), pulled the property up live, honestly suggested foam leveling for the repair, asked for photos and gave a $5k to $7k ballpark. Missed: rambling and inconsistent scope talk, said pavers were 'out of my wheelhouse', budget question came late, and no next step was booked. Photos still not received.

Good qualifying (15x17 sunken living room, 6 in. fill, access and furniture) and helpful education on why a $3k bid is risky, which builds trust. Missed: quoted about $8k then $5.5k in the same call, which hurt credibility; her budget (~$3k) wasn't asked until after pricing. Correct outcome: fair disqualification, marked Lost.

Very fast callback and a quick 120 sq ft range ($3,750 to $4,500) for a 12x10 patio extension that's already framed. Missed: he said he wants to book right away, but the call ended with no site visit, no proposal and no follow-up date. Opp went to Lost the same day with no note. Next time: when a buyer says 'right away', book it on the call.

Strong: let Bill explain, explored tear-out vs. resurface, covered stamped, colored and pavers, got a budget ($20k to $25k), and booked Tue 10/27 10 to 12 with a 30-minute heads-up promise. Missed: no driveway/walkway size or photo request, and he left it unclear who's coming ('my tech Nehemiah or the owner'). The visit is not on any GHL calendar yet.

Fast first callback (~25 hrs after the AI-receptionist intake) and an efficient call: opened with the context of his request, restated scope (22x6 ft tear-out/replace), offered a concrete slot (Tue noon), confirmed the street address and cross-street, and asked permission to text a reminder. Missed: no qualification at all before committing a Tucson drive: never asked budget, timeline, or whether it's a tear-out vs. a bridge/overlay (he raised both options and Joshua just said 'yes'); never mentioned the $2,500 minimum or asked for photos to pre-qualify; didn't explain what the visit/estimate includes; said 'have a great weekend' on a Thursday. He cancelled by phone 3 hours later, so a 30-second budget/photo check would have saved the slot. Coaching: before booking out-of-area visits, ask 'roughly what budget are you thinking?' and 'can you text me 2-3 photos?'

New Angi pickleball-court lead; called back within about an hour of the after-hours lead (VM + text, then reached him when he called in). Strong rapport and real expertise: explained the 28-day cure before coating, 5" monolithic slab, base + vapor barrier, and used live social proof (courts pouring this week in Arcadia and Queen Creek). Gave a clear ballpark (~$20-22k at 5", ~$17k at 4" for ~30x60). Missed: never offered a free site visit or written quote, didn't get the address, didn't ask budget or anchor value against the $50k quote he'd heard, and when he said 'not until next year' didn't test financing, off-season pricing or a dated next step. Offered to show a court but didn't set it up. Rep introduced himself as 'Tim'; call logged under Nehemiah's GHL user. Opp moved to Long-Term Nurture; recap task with draft due today 3 PM.

Follow-up call on the $23,226 garage + gazebo slab estimate. Called when promised, friendly and to the point, and locked a clear next step: Tony is waiting on his GC's turnkey vs. concrete-only split (expected by end of week), so call back Thursday. Missed: didn't ask what will decide it (price, schedule, one contractor vs. two), didn't offer to sharpen or walk through our concrete-only number, and didn't check on the city red-line approval from his earlier notes. CRM: no opportunity exists yet — create one; WATCHMAN proposal task due today 10 AM; approved plans are in the TC@zreigroup.com inbox.
